record.paper_title: Minimal positive realizations: a survey of recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Given a positive realization of a transfer function, how can one approximate it by another positive realization of lower state dimension while preserving the positivity constraints and remaining close to the original system behavior?

evidence.quote: - how can one approximate a positive realization by a lower dimension one?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G(z)$ be a rational transfer function of a discrete-time single-input single-output linear time-invariant system, and suppose
$$G(z) = C(zI_n - A)^{-1}B + D$$
is a positive realization of dimension $n$, meaning that the entries of $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$, $B \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times 1}$, $C \in \mathbb{R}^{1\times n}$, and $D \in \mathbb{R}$ are all nonnegative (so that, for any nonnegative input sequence and nonnegative initial state, the state trajectory and output remain nonnegative).

Develop a constructive procedure that, given such a positive realization $(A,B,C,D)$ of dimension $n$ and a tolerance $\varepsilon > 0$, produces another positive realization $(\tilde A, \tilde B, \tilde C, \tilde D)$ of dimension $\tilde n < n$ (with all entries of $\tilde A, \tilde B, \tilde C, \tilde D$ nonnegative) such that the corresponding transfer function $\tilde G(z) = \tilde C(zI_{\tilde n} - \tilde A)^{-1}\tilde B + \tilde D$ approximates $G(z)$ in a prescribed system norm, e.g.
$$\|G - \tilde G\|_{\mathcal H_\infty} \le \varepsilon \quad\text{or}\quad \|G - \tilde G\|_{\mathcal H_2} \le \varepsilon.$$

Equivalently: characterize, for a given positive system, the smallest dimension $\tilde n$ achievable by a positive approximant within tolerance $\varepsilon$, and provide an algorithm that attains it while preserving nonnegativity of all matrices.
artifact.status_search_result: Model reduction for general linear systems is a well-studied area (balanced truncation, Krylov, POD), but reduction that strictly preserves nonnegativity (positivity) of the realization matrices remains an active research topic. Even computing the minimal-dimension positive realization of a given transfer function is a known open problem, and recent work (e.g., 2025 work on minimal positive Markov realizations) shows that constructive minimum-dimension positive approximation is not generally resolved.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive Markov realizations (arXiv:2502.21102)
status_evidence.snippet: Finding a positive state-space realization with the minimum dimension for a given transfer function is an open problem in control theory. A linear programming approach is proposed that focuses on positive realizations in Markov form.
status_evidence.claim: Minimum-dimension positive realization is acknowledged as an open problem; recent partial approaches address restricted (Markov) cases.

status_evidence.title: Model order reduction - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Model order reduction aims to lower the computational complexity... preserving structure such as positivity is highlighted as a desirable but nontrivial property.
status_evidence.claim: Structure-preserving (including positivity-preserving) model reduction is recognized as a separate, harder problem than general MOR.
